capability: Fail closed across Version state, inventory, source-check, and automatic-prompt projection when durable authority is unusable
searchEvidence: Trace ReloadDurableCurrentWithoutLockAsync, PublishStateUnavailable, PublishInventoryUnavailable, RequireCurrentWithoutLockAsync, CheckAsync, SettingsViewModel.ApplyVersionSnapshot, and MainWindow.RunVersionDiscoveryAfterReadyAsync across src and tests

Verify Invalid, Unavailable, managed-root mismatch, writer-lease failure, durable-save failure, and inventory-read failure after a prior catalog, verified candidate, prompt, release-notes disclosure, and retention action

Verify writer-contention recovery after another writer changes the durable active version: cached catalog may support direct retry, but connected status, verified candidate, generation, and automatic prompt stay cleared until a fresh check
Require one Application fail-closed snapshot contract plus presentation-only suppression; prohibit catalog or package probing while state or inventory authority is unusable
semanticOwner: VersionManagementExperience owns terminal usable-state and usable-inventory authority; Presentation consumes that snapshot and independently suppresses unusable automatic prompts
terminalContract: Any unavailable durable state or inventory publishes an empty unavailable inventory, no public catalog, no verified candidate, no automatic prompt, no connected source claim, and no actionable version rows. Check does not access catalog or package adapters until both authorities are usable. A private same-source catalog may survive transient writer contention only for the existing direct install retry; recovery never republishes connected status, verified candidate, generation, or prompt, and a changed active version invalidates candidate context. Missing durable state remains the sole intentional empty bootstrap. MainWindow cannot open Settings automatically from an unusable snapshot, and release-note, confirmation, retention, and row projections are cleared.

designReview.evidence: Independent R2 evidence review found that PublishStateUnavailable retained stale inventory, catalog, candidate and prompt facts, while CheckAsync and MainWindow could still consume them. The correction centralizes fail-closed authority in Application and retains only a presentation defense at the automatic prompt boundary.
